query: We're a 12-person startup and I want to hire our first salesperson. I've never hired for sales before. How should I run this so I don't screw it up?
expected_behavior: Starts with a scorecard: a one-line mission, three to six measurable, ranked outcomes (a revenue number and a date), and the competencies that predict them, framed as outcomes rather than responsibilities
Plans sourcing from the funnel backward, distinguishing outbound from inbound and standing up a referral engine, since a first sales hire is almost always outbound
Designs a structured loop with a coverage matrix and a work sample (for example a mock discovery call), where every interviewer scores independently against a written rubric
Requires evidence-based evaluation with independent scores committed before the debrief, and recommends a bar raiser or an outside voice to hold the bar
Includes reference checks as a real gate and an offer built on a comp band, then a 30/60/90 onboarding plan mapped to the scorecard outcomes with an engineered first win
Does not jump straight to interview questions or job-board posts before the scorecard exists
